pulls.title: 8392811: C2 with lock elimination throws NPE for field store through conditional receiver
pulls.author: JohnTortugo
pulls.body_excerpt: Please, review this patch to fix `NullPointerException` thrown by C2 generated code. The problem occur when an object is the merge pointer of a `SafePointScalarMerge` in an EA iteration become scalar replaceable in subsequent EA iterations - e.g., because its lock is eliminated, which happens only after EA iteration runs. During a deoptimization the merge pointer is read as an `oop` before the scalar replaced objects are reallocated, so it is seen as null and the following field store (or monitor enter) throws. The fix I'm proposing makes `can_eliminate_allocation` return false for allocations

pulls.author: cushon
pulls.body_excerpt: This change adds Vector API methods that load the code units of a `java.lang.String` into a vector without copying, to allow processing a `String` with a vector loop instead of a scalar loop over `charAt`. As discussed in the [panama-dev@ thread 'String processing and Vector APIs'](https://mail.openjdk.org/archives/list/panama-dev@openjdk.org/thread/YSPX3TBXZTZEFZNXWDYOZCWLUQPC62P6/), one motivating use-case is a regex library that wants to accelerate scans for character classes. Implementing these methods outside the JDK using scalar `charAt` loops is slower than a vectorized implementation.

pulls.title: 8374307: Fix deoptimization storm caused by Action_none in GraphKit::uncommon_trap
pulls.author: bulasevich
pulls.body_excerpt: We observed a deoptimization storm caused by GraphKit::uncommon_trap generator logic. GraphKit::uncommon_trap considers the too_many_recompiles metric. If the threshold is overflowed, it replaces Deoptimization::Action_reinterpret with Deoptimization::Action_none (see code snippet below). This replacement changes the uncommon_trap logic: once execution hits a trap, the VM performs deoptimization but does not recompile the method anymore. In an "unlucky" case, when the code part calling this uncommon_trap becomes frequent, a deoptimization storm occurs (thousands of deoptimizations per second)
